verdict.summary: The research step returned no sourced findings, so this guide is based on general knowledge and every point is marked 'inferred'. As generally understood, a GitHub OAuth App works for any GitHub user as soon as you create it, with no review. The main thing that can block you is an organization's OAuth app access restrictions, which require an org owner to approve your app.
verdict.approval_wait: none (inferred; only the optional GitHub Marketplace listing is reviewed)

gates.name: OAuth App created (owner account)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own GitHub account through your app via Composio.
limits: Unverified: no test or sandbox mode is known; the app is live as soon as you create it.

gates.name: Same OAuth App, shared with other users
gates.unlocks: Any invited user can authorize. There is no separate test-user allowlist.
limits: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must approve the app before org resources can be accessed (inferred).

gates.name: Public use (optional Marketplace listing)
gates.unlocks: Any GitHub user can authorize. A Marketplace listing only adds discoverability.
limits: The org approval requirement still applies per organization (inferred).
Marketplace listing is optional and reviewed by GitHub (inferred).
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for public authorization; Marketplace review timing unknown

steps.title: Sign in to the GitHub account or org that will own the app
steps.detail: Decide whether the app should belong to your personal account or an organization. For a production agent, organization ownership is usually better so the app doesn't depend on one person's account (inferred).

steps.title: Open Developer settings > OAuth Apps
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps and click 'New OAuth App'. For an org-owned app, use the organization's Settings > Developer settings instead.
gotchas: GitHub also offers 'GitHub Apps', which are a different model with fine-grained permissions. Make sure your Composio auth config expects an OAuth App (unverified).

steps.title: Fill in the app registration form
steps.detail: Enter Application name, Homepage URL, an optional Application description, and the Authorization callback URL. For the callback URL, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: OAuth Apps are generally understood to accept only one callback URL, so it must match exactly (inferred).

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: After you register the app, copy the Client ID, click 'Generate a new client secret', and copy the secret right away because GitHub shows it only once (inferred).

steps.title: Choose the scopes your agent needs
steps.detail: List the GitHub API actions your agent performs and map them to the smallest set of OAuth scopes, e.g. read:user and user:email for identity, and repo only if you need private repository access. GitHub scopes are requested at authorization time, not set in the app form (inferred).

steps.title: Add the credentials to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the GitHub toolkit using your own OAuth credentials. Paste the Client ID and Client Secret and set the scopes you chose.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a connection in Composio, approve the GitHub consent screen with your own account, and call a simple endpoint such as GET /user to confirm the token works.

steps.title: Ask org owners to approve the app if needed
steps.detail: If users need access to repositories in organizations that have OAuth app access restrictions, they request approval during authorization and an org owner approves it under the org's third-party access settings (inferred).

steps.title: (Optional) List on GitHub Marketplace
steps.detail: Public users can already authorize your app without a listing. List on GitHub Marketplace only if you want discoverability. Listing requires a submission that GitHub reviews (inferred).

requirements.detail: Needed to register an OAuth App (inferred).
Required fields on the registration form. The callback URL must exactly match the Composio callback URL (inferred).
Only required for organizations that have OAuth app access restrictions turned on (inferred).

scopes.effect: Gives read access to profile and email. No review (inferred).
Gives full access to private repositories. No review is required, but users see a broad-permission consent screen (inferred).

blockers.symptom: Authorization succeeds, but the organization's repositories are missing or return 404/403
blockers.cause: The organization has OAuth app access restrictions and hasn't approved your app (inferred).
blockers.fix: Have the user request access, and have an org owner approve the app in the organization's third-party application access settings.

blockers.symptom: 'The redirect_uri MUST match the registered callback URL for this application' error
blockers.cause: The Authorization callback URL doesn't match the URL Composio sends (inferred).
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the OAuth App's Authorization callback URL field.

composio.note: The research didn't confirm Composio's GitHub toolkit details. You can usually start on managed auth if Composio offers it. Switch to your own OAuth App when you want your own app name and logo on the consent screen, your own rate-limit and org-approval relationship, or exact control over scopes. On GitHub this switch takes about 15 minutes and needs no review (inferred).

evidence.claim: GitHub OAuth Apps are created under Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps with name, homepage URL and callback URL fields, and work at once without review.
GitHub OAuth scopes such as read:user, user:email and repo are requested at authorization time and don't trigger app review.
Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must approve an OAuth App before it can access org resources.
GitHub Marketplace listing is optional and goes through GitHub review. It isn't needed for public authorization.
Composio lets you supply your own OAuth client ID and secret in an auth config.

open_questions: The research run returned no findings. Every claim here is inferred and should be checked against GitHub's docs (docs.github.com OAuth Apps pages).
Unconfirmed: Composio's GitHub toolkit slug, whether managed OAuth is available, and its default scopes.
Unconfirmed: whether Composio's GitHub integration expects an OAuth App or a GitHub App.
Unconfirmed: current token expiry behavior for OAuth App tokens, and whether OAuth Apps support more than one callback URL.
Unknown: GitHub Marketplace review requirements and timeline, if you want a listing.
